node.title: Re: pass a variable or string to shell command from perl script (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
First of all, [marto] is right that you don't need to call an external command for this, there is [doc://mkdir], and also make_path from the core module [doc://File::Path] (Update: which can do the equivalent of mkdir -p). For proper handling of filenames, see the core module [doc://File::Spec], or, with a nicer interface, [mod://Path::Class] from CPAN.

use File::Spec::Functions qw/catdir/; use File::Path qw/make_path/; make_path(catdir('folderA','folderB','folderC')); # Update 2: OR: use Path::Class qw/dir/; dir('folderA','folderB','folderC')->mkpath;

Only for the sake of completeness: I wrote about different ways to call external commmands (safely) at length [id://1180578|here].
